clue.text: Casual tuna Nicoise salad with no end of mayonnaise

indicators.note: a salad is a mixture of ingredients tossed together, so the letters of the fish dish are tossed into a new order
the end of a word is its final letter, here the last letter of mayonnaise

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a tuna Nicoise salad made without the dressing it normally ends with.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a composite anagram: the letters of TUNA NICOISE, once the E (end of 'mayonnaise') is taken away, are rearranged by 'salad'.
explanation.definitionFit: Insouciant describes a carefree, offhand attitude, which is what casual means of a person's manner.

clue.text: One old-fashioned star

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make something, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone describes a film star from a bygone era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' reads as one adjective, but 'fashioned' is the anagram signal working on I plus OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A star of film or music is a celebrity adored by fans, which is exactly what an idol is.

clue.text: Underwater mud grebes churned up

indicators.note: churning up stirs and mixes things, so the letters are stirred into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Grebes diving in a lake stir up the mud below the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something submerged has gone under the surface, so it lies beneath the water.

clue.text: Absolute lunatic losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a nutter is informal British slang for a lunatic

explanation.surface: Someone calls another person a complete lunatic who has lost their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter and absolute are synonyms as intensifiers, as in utter nonsense or absolute nonsense.

clue.text: Trendy parties — outside or not outside

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy

indicators.note: the word outside here says the parties word wraps around the little word or

parts.note: dos are parties, as in a big do
taken as written

explanation.surface: A host debates whether a fashionable party should be held in the garden or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' appears twice: the first is the container signal, the second is part of the definition 'not outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inside a building means not being outdoors, so the phrase 'not outside' fits exactly.

clue.text: New advancement starting to develop

parts.note: an ascent is a rise or advancement

explanation.surface: A fresh promotion at work is just beginning to take shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into existence, so something nascent is beginning to grow or develop.

clue.text: 'Wrack' is Emerson, Lake and Palmer touching rock bottom

indicators.note: touching means sitting beside, so the band's letters adjoin the rock letter
the bottom of a word is its final letter, so rock gives its end

parts.note: ELP is the usual abbreviation for the prog rock band Emerson, Lake and Palmer

explanation.surface: A music critic says the prog band have reached their lowest point in rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock bottom' reads as the lowest point, but 'bottom' simply takes the last letter of 'rock'.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrack is coarse seaweed washed up on shore, and kelp is a large brown seaweed, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Practise extortion to be precise

definitions.meaning: to ... money is to demand and extract it by force

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning to extort payment and an adjective meaning accurate.

clue.text: Firm taking time to go into profit for speculator

indicators.note: to go into means to enter, so the firm with its time sits inside the profit word

parts.note: to prosper is to profit or thrive

indicators.note: taking means the firm word holds the time letter within it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A business takes its time before moving into making money as a speculator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'profit' looks like a noun but is a verb; 'taking' puts time inside the firm, and 'to go into' sends that into the profit word.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospector searches for gold or oil hoping to strike it rich, a kind of speculator.

clue.text: Carefree broadcasting under leadership of Digital European Bureau

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means placed below, so it comes after
the leadership of a group of words is their initial letters

parts.note: on air means being broadcast

explanation.surface: A European digital broadcasting body is run in a relaxed manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes someone suave and lighthearted, so it means carefree in manner.

clue.text: Gold coin in circulation

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
a bit is a small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: A gold coin is passing from hand to hand in general use.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is a circular path around something, so it describes circulation or going round.

clue.text: Rail about peers turning out criminal

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the rail word surrounds the rearranged peers

parts.note: a dado is a rail along an interior wall, as in a dado rail

indicators.note: turning out suggests producing something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rails at members of the House of Lords for turning out to be crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' looks like a verb meaning complain, but it is a noun, the rail along a wall; 'turning out' rearranges the peers and 'about' wraps the rail round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, so the word means a criminal.

clue.text: Loud organ gets a little frightening

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
the ear is an organ of hearing
some means a small amount

explanation.surface: A loud church organ is getting somewhat scary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the musical instrument, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fearsome inspires fear, so it is frightening.

clue.text: Always available for panto performance

indicators.note: a performance can be a fuss or production, signalling the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A Christmas pantomime show that is always ready to put on.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto is a British Christmas pantomime, a comic family stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer that is on tap flows freely whenever wanted, so the idiom means always available.

clue.text: Note that is about 40% of Mancunians consuming fortified wine

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the letters for 'that is' surround everything else

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the fragment of Mancunians holds the wine
forty percent of a ten-letter word is its first four letters

parts.note: port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: A remark that many people from Manchester are drinking port.
explanation.walkthrough: Mancunians are people from Manchester; '40% of' takes four of its ten letters. 'consuming' puts the wine inside, and 'about' wraps 'that is' round everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Note can mean significance, as in a person of note, which is importance.

clue.text: Silly me sing badly? By gum, that's got about

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word gum is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of sing are put in a poor, jumbled order

explanation.surface: Someone sings out of tune and exclaims 'By gum!' at their own mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By gum' is a Northern English exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggins is British slang for oneself as a fool, as in 'muggins here has to pay', so it means silly me.

clue.text: Fearless Republican getting lukewarm reception after putting home first

indicators.note: putting home first means the home word comes at the start

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: a reception takes something in, so the lukewarm word receives the Republican letter

parts.note: tepid means lukewarm

explanation.surface: A bold Republican gets a cool welcome after prioritising domestic matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means bold and undaunted by danger, the same as fearless.

clue.text: Transport service following in sudden movement

indicators.note: in means placed inside the word for a sudden movement

parts.note: a tic is a sudden involuntary twitch
the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A transport service is described as following a jerky motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic is the movement of vehicles or goods, so it can mean transport.

clue.text: Pulse of unfinished Follett novel capturing era

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the rearranged name contains the era word
novel means new or unusual, so the letters are put in a new order
unfinished means the name loses its final letter

parts.note: an age is an era

explanation.surface: A Ken Follett novel left incomplete takes in a whole historical period.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Follett is a bestselling novelist. FOLLET, rearranged by 'novel' as FLOLET, takes in AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A flageolet is a small French kidney bean, and pulses are the edible seeds of legumes.

clue.text: Grandad dropping cold stern exterior

indicators.note: dropping the exterior means shedding the outer letters, leaving the inside of the phrase
dropping the exterior means shedding the outer letters, leaving the inside of the phrase

explanation.surface: An elderly man is softening his cold, stern manner.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldster is an old person, and a grandad is typically one.

clue.text: Take drink in silence after umpire deducted two points

indicators.note: after means the silence word comes later than the umpire's remains
deducted means taken away, so the points are removed from the umpire word

parts.note: a referee is an umpire
E is east, a compass point, so two points give two Es
sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: A player quietly has a drink after the umpire docks two points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' suggests a score, but here they are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh oneself is to take a drink or food to revive.

clue.text: Commotion involving amateur sailors ordered about in hurricane

indicators.note: involving means containing, so the commotion word wraps around the rest

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion

indicators.note: ordered about means rearranged, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, the sailors

explanation.surface: Amateur sailors bossed around in a storm cause a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent whirling windstorm, much like a hurricane.

clue.text: Appropriate time to wake up — right?

parts.note: to rouse is to wake up

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is a suitable time to get up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb: to trouser money is British slang for pocketing it.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser something is informal for pocketing it, taking it for oneself, which is to appropriate it.

clue.text: Palate manifesting refinement

definitions.meaning: a palate is a sense of flavour

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the sense of flavour and discerning judgement in aesthetic matters.

clue.text: Naïve beginner appearing in sketch is poor

indicators.note: appearing in means placed inside, so the letter goes within the sketch word

parts.note: a skit is a short comic sketch

indicators.note: the beginner of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A naive newcomer performing in a comedy sketch has no money.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Skint is British informal for penniless, so it means poor.

clue.text: Fish go to the bottom to devour last of krill

indicators.note: to devour is to swallow, so the sinking word takes the letter inside

parts.note: to founder is to sink to the bottom

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A fish dives to the seabed to feed on krill.
explanation.definitionFit: A flounder is a flatfish, so it is a kind of fish.

clue.text: Could be goat starts to meander over the heath

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A goat wanders across the heath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goat' suggests the animal, but the goat moth is a large moth species.
explanation.definitionFit: The goat moth is a species of moth, so a goat could be an example of one.

clue.text: One with overriding tendency to pry creating clamour

indicators.note: overriding means riding over and around, so the prying word covers the letter

parts.note: nosiness is a tendency to pry
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A dominant urge to snoop creates an uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisiness is a loud racket, a synonym for clamour.

clue.text: Incumbent's first good look round White House

indicators.note: the first of a word is its initial letter

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A new president takes a tour of the White House.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White House' suggests the president's home, but here it is a house made of snow blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped house built of snow, hence a white house.

clue.text: 'Repast' is regularly 'nosh'

indicators.note: regularly means picking letters at regular intervals, every other one

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry claims that repast commonly means nosh.
explanation.walkthrough: Nosh is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats and nosh are both informal slang words for food.

clue.text: The orchids flourish in a part of London

indicators.note: to flourish is to grow or wave about, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Orchids are thriving in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOREDITCH is a fashionable district in East London.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoreditch is a district of the London Borough of Hackney.
